articles.headline: BJP reshuffle may set course for cabinet rejig
articles.summary: The BJP has announced a new organizational team, including the return of Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani to national roles. This reshuffle, involving 13 vice-presidents and nine general secretaries, is seen as a precursor to a potential Union cabinet expansion by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

articles.headline: NTA ordered to audit all exam processes, give report
articles.summary: The Union education ministry has directed the National Testing Agency (NTA) to conduct a thorough audit of its examination processes and submit a report on corrective action within 30 days. This follows widespread concerns over irregularities in national-level entrance tests like UGC-NET.

articles.headline: Tughlakabad may face most cuts in Delhi SIR
articles.summary: The first phase of Delhi's special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls shows that Tughlakabad might see the highest percentage of name deletions. Officials are identifying voters who are dead, shifted, or absent to ensure the accuracy of the voter list before the next elections.

articles.headline: Black money in polls: SC sets 1-yr probe deadline
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated a one-year deadline for completing investigations into the use of black money and other inducements in elections. The court directed high courts to designate special courts for the speedy trial of electoral offenses to maintain democratic integrity.

articles.headline: Soren govt accepts protesters' demand, cancels key exams
articles.summary: The Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand government has cancelled the JSSC-CGL examination and other recruitment tests following intense protests by students. The protesters had alleged irregularities and demanded a CBI probe into the exam process conducted by a private firm.

articles.headline: WB hotel fire kills 9 as locked exits trap guests
articles.summary: A massive fire at a hotel in West Bengal's Birbhum district killed nine people, including two children. Preliminary reports suggest the fire was caused by a short circuit, and casualties were high because emergency exits were allegedly locked or blocked with furniture.

articles.headline: Unemployment rate in 15-29 yrs age group rises marginally
articles.summary: Data from the National Statistical Office (NSO) shows that the unemployment rate for the 15-29 age group in urban areas rose slightly to 5.1% in July. The increase is attributed to more people entering the workforce, although the labor force participation rate also showed an upward trend.

articles.headline: Taliban pitches deeper India ties at 'Victory Day' reception
articles.summary: The Taliban regime in Afghanistan hosted its first-ever public reception on Indian soil to mark its third anniversary of returning to power. The event aimed to send a message of deeper engagement with India on regional stability, trade, and economic cooperation.

articles.headline: Top court bars ED, CBI from filing reports in Rahul case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has stayed an Allahabad High Court order that directed the CBI and ED to submit progress reports on an investigation into the assets of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. The top court questioned the necessity of such a probe if no formal FIR had been registered.

articles.headline: DGCA weighs wider drug testing for pilots
articles.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is considering expanding random drug testing for all pilots across domestic airlines. This follows an incident where a pilot allegedly failed a preliminary drug test, raising concerns about safety standards in the aviation industry.

articles.headline: Vijay unveils full waiver of crop loans up to ₹75k
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has announced a full waiver of cooperative crop loans of up to ₹75,000 for farmers in the state. The move is expected to benefit over 1.4 million farmers and will cost the state exchequer approximately ₹5,933 crore.

articles.headline: Twisha case: Ex-judge, her son named for abetment of suicide
articles.summary: Former actor Twisha Sharma's mother-in-law, a former district judge, and her husband have been booked for abetment of suicide. The CBI filed a charge sheet alleging that the 33-year-old was subjected to mental harassment and dowry demands before her death in May.

articles.headline: U.S. not looking to extend Iran deal: Trump
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has stated that his administration is not seeking an extension of the 60-day memorandum of understanding with Iran regarding its nuclear program. Trump emphasized that any future deal would have to be more comprehensive and address Iran's regional activities.

articles.headline: Soap opera unfolds in NE war against drugs
articles.summary: Law enforcement agencies in Northeast India are intensifying their crackdown on drug trafficking, uncovering various methods used by smugglers, including the use of soap cases to hide narcotics. The region remains a major transit point for drugs entering from the Golden Triangle.

articles.headline: Skymet cuts monsoon forecast to 85% of LPA
articles.summary: Private forecaster Skymet Weather has downgraded its monsoon forecast for India, predicting rainfall at 85% of the Long Period Average (LPA). The revision is due to the strengthening of El Nino conditions, which could lead to a significant deficit in the latter half of the season.

articles.headline: UK’s Burnham exchanged messages with Trump aide imposter
articles.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham exchanged messages with someone posing as a senior aide to Donald Trump. The imposter reportedly sought to influence discussions on international matters, prompting a security review into how such a breach occurred.

articles.headline: SC to hear NBCC plea for Supertech projects
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has agreed to examine a plea by NBCC (India) Limited regarding the completion of stalled Supertech housing projects. NBCC is seeking directions to take over several projects to ensure that thousands of homebuyers finally receive their promised apartments.

articles.headline: Jadeja joins elite 350 wickets, 4k runs club
articles.summary: Indian all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja has entered an elite group of cricketers by reaching 350 Test wickets and 4,000 runs. He achieved this feat during the match against Sri Lanka, becoming only the fifth Indian and the fastest left-arm spinner to reach the 350-wicket milestone.

articles.headline: Star of 'Heroes' and 'Nashville' dies at 36
articles.summary: Actor and singer Hayden Panettiere, known for her roles in the television series 'Heroes' and 'Nashville,' has passed away at the age of 36. Her family confirmed the news, remembering her as a talented performer who captured the hearts of many with her work.

articles.headline: Trump scales back South Korea military drills
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has decided to significantly scale back joint military exercises with South Korea. The move is intended as a diplomatic gesture toward North Korea to encourage further talks on denuclearization, although it has raised security concerns among allies.

articles.headline: Quest to regain movement, one robot at a time
articles.summary: Researchers are making significant strides in developing wearable robotic exoskeletons to help individuals with paralysis regain mobility. These advanced systems use sensors and AI to interpret muscle signals, allowing users to walk and perform daily activities more independently.

articles.headline: Transport minister hints at bus fare hike in Karnataka
articles.summary: Karnataka Transport Minister Ramalinga Reddy has indicated a potential hike in bus fares for state-run transport corporations. The minister cited rising diesel prices and the need to cover operational losses as the primary reasons for the proposed increase.

articles.headline: State expands food safety inspections, launches QR code
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has expanded food safety inspections to include more restaurants and eateries. A new QR code-based system has been launched to allow citizens to easily report complaints and check the safety ratings of food establishments.

articles.headline: 7.3 million names not included in Telangana draft rolls
articles.summary: The draft electoral rolls for Telangana have revealed that over 7.3 million names have been removed during the special intensive revision. Election officials stated that the deletions include deceased, shifted, or duplicate voters, but opposition parties have raised concerns.

articles.headline: Kerala Police loosens uniform regulations for pregnant cops
articles.summary: In a progressive move, the Kerala Police department has relaxed its uniform regulations for pregnant police officers. The new guidelines allow them to wear comfortable, non-restrictive clothing instead of the standard uniform while on duty.

articles.headline: TTD begins total overhaul of accounting, fiscal systems
articles.summary: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) has initiated a comprehensive overhaul of its accounting and fiscal management systems. The project aims to improve transparency and efficiency in the management of the temple's vast financial resources.

articles.headline: Pak-based terror network thwarted before I-Day: Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that a major Pakistan-based terror network was busted ahead of Independence Day. Security forces arrested several individuals and seized a cache of arms and explosives intended for attacks across multiple states.

articles.headline: Website lets users report bribes in India anonymously
articles.summary: A new website has been launched that allows Indian citizens to report instances of bribery anonymously. The platform aims to collect data on corruption across various government departments to help identify systemic issues and push for transparency.

articles.headline: Self-enumeration phase of census in snow-bound areas
articles.summary: The government has launched a self-enumeration phase for the national census in remote, snow-bound areas. This initiative allows residents in challenging terrains to provide their information online, ensuring data collection before door-to-door visits.

articles.headline: Court flags lapses in curbing child sexual abuse content
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has expressed concern over lapses by platforms in curbing the spread of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The court directed the government to enforce stricter regulations and ensure the immediate removal of such harmful content.

articles.headline: Transgender IDs to be valid till verdict on new law
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that existing identity cards for transgender persons will remain valid until it reaches a final verdict on the constitutionality of a new law. This interim order ensures that individuals continue to access benefits and services.

articles.headline: Pakistan detains 258 foreigners in scam centre raid
articles.summary: Pakistani authorities have detained 258 foreign nationals during a raid on an illegal call center. The facility was allegedly being used to run various online scams and fraudulent investment schemes targeting victims globally.

articles.headline: Thousands await aid after quake kills 68 in Indonesia
articles.summary: Thousands of people in Indonesia are waiting for emergency aid after a powerful earthquake killed at least 68 people. Rescue operations are ongoing in the affected regions, but heavy rains have hampered relief and medical efforts.

articles.headline: Nvidia set to back OpenAI project with $10.5bn funding
articles.summary: Tech giant Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest $10.5 billion into a major new OpenAI project. The funding would support the development of next-generation AI models and the infrastructure needed to power complex artificial intelligence applications.

articles.headline: Small firms could get big relief on bank guarantees
articles.summary: The Indian government is considering a proposal to ease the burden of bank guarantees for small and medium enterprises (SMEs). The plan could involve reducing the required guarantee amounts, potentially freeing up significant capital for business expansion.

articles.headline: Razorpay builds AI model to improve payment success rates
articles.summary: Fintech major Razorpay has developed a new AI-powered model designed to significantly improve the success rates of digital payments. The system uses machine learning to identify and resolve transaction failures in real-time, benefiting merchants and customers.

articles.headline: Centre plans to scrap performance bank guarantees for MSMEs
articles.summary: The Union government is considering replacing stiff performance bank guarantees for MSMEs in government contracts with existing credit guarantee schemes. This policy shift, discussed by the MSME ministry and DPIIT, aims to free up trillions of rupees in working capital. MSMEs currently account for 30% of India's GDP and half of the central government’s ₹2.30 trillion procurement in FY26.

articles.headline: Microsoft and Salesforce eye buyout of HR software firm Darwinbox
articles.summary: Global tech giants Microsoft, Salesforce, and ADP have reportedly approached HR firm Darwinbox for a potential buyout. The KKR-backed firm was valued at $1 billion last year and has raised $290 million to date. While Darwinbox officially plans for a medium-term IPO, strategic investors are looking to add its payroll and people analytics expertise to their software suites.

articles.headline: India's retail sector sees mixed growth amid raw material inflation
articles.summary: The retail consumer sector reported strong Q1FY27 performance in rural and premium FMCG segments, though raw material price hikes caused by West Asia tensions weighed on results. While firms like V-Mart saw profit jumps, Avenue Supermarts faced subdued growth due to operating costs. Companies expect a stronger performance in upcoming quarters due to an extended festival window.

articles.headline: US-Iran deadlock continues over Strait of Hormuz shipping chokepoint
articles.summary: Tensions remain high as the US and Iran bin their June truce memorandum, leaving the status of the Strait of Hormuz uncertain. Both nations claim control over the vital oil shipping lane, which has seen traffic reduced to a trickle. The world must resolve this obstruction before global oil reserves run thin and crude prices face a potential after-shock.

articles.headline: Over 40% of landless PMAY-G beneficiaries still await land allocation
articles.summary: More than 40% of landless beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin have not yet received land, according to rural development ministry data. Karnataka has the highest pendency at 97.8%, while Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh have performed better. The delays in land identification remain a critical hurdle for housing targets in several Indian states.

articles.headline: UPI transaction value reaches 70% of India's cash in circulation
articles.summary: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has become the world’s largest digital payment system, with transaction values now equivalent to 70% of India's currency in circulation. Data from PhonePe shows Bengaluru Urban is the top district for transactions. While digital payments are spreading beyond major cities, richer states still show higher concentration and usage levels than poorer ones.

articles.headline: Permira frontrunner to acquire $200 million stake in Cloudnine Hospitals
articles.summary: Global private equity fund Permira is reportedly leading the race to acquire a $150-200 million stake in Bengaluru-based maternal healthcare chain Cloudnine. The deal is expected to be secondary in nature, with investor True North selling its decade-old stake. Cloudnine operates 40 centers across India and recently acquired Apollo Health & Lifestyle’s childcare business.

articles.headline: Ather Energy and Hero MotoCorp monetize software features for revenue
articles.summary: Electric scooter makers Ather Energy and Hero MotoCorp are focusing on digital 'tech packs' to boost non-vehicle revenue. Ather’s software-led earnings now account for 14% of its total revenue, helping it break even at the operating-profit level. Features like advanced navigation, voice commands, and predictive safety are being sold as high-margin add-ons to traditional hardware.

articles.headline: India's art auction turnover jumps 43% led by modern masters
articles.summary: The Indian art auction market saw a 43.7% year-on-year jump in turnover to ₹1,548 crore in H1CY26. The growth is driven by high prices for a small pool of modern masters like M.F. Husain and Raja Ravi Varma rather than sales volume. The number of lots fetching over ₹1 crore rose 35%, reflecting strong demand for high-quality, rare works with established provenance.

articles.headline: Centre to finalize new airfare rules under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam
articles.summary: The Union government told the Supreme Court it has fast-tracked the framing of rules to modernize India’s aviation sector. The new rules, aimed at addressing airfare transparency and modernization, will be finalized within three weeks. The draft rules were placed before the court in a sealed cover as final discussions continue between relevant ministries.

articles.headline: India's soyoil imports set for record high amid war disruptions
articles.summary: Soyoil imports are projected to reach a record 620,000 tonnes in August as competitive prices and festive demand drive purchases. The Russia-Ukraine war has disrupted sunflower oil shipments, prompting Indian refiners to switch oils. Current import levels are nearly 46% above the average monthly intake for the current marketing year.

articles.headline: Sebi chairman says closing auction session is here to stay
articles.summary: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey confirmed that the newly introduced closing auction session (CAS) for securities is permanent, despite criticism over low liquidity. The regulator will examine and address constraints in the mechanism but will not abandon it. CAS aims to align India's markets with global practices to improve price discovery and reduce settlement stress.

articles.headline: Bihar joins Centre's direct pulse procurement network for the first time
articles.summary: Bihar has joined the central government's direct procurement network for masoor (lentils), allowing central agencies to buy directly from farmers instead of state intermediaries. As of August, 3,000 tonnes have been procured at the MSP of ₹7,000 per quintal. The move aims to establish farmer confidence in the Centre's procurement mechanism and boost pulse cultivation in the state.

articles.headline: Anurag Jain takes charge as new CEO of Niti Aayog
articles.summary: Senior IAS officer Anurag Jain has been appointed the Chief Executive Officer of Niti Aayog for a two-year term. Jain previously served as the secretary for the ministry of road transport and highways. He succeeds B.V.R. Subrahmanyam. His appointment is expected to improve coordination between the central government and states while supporting national development priorities.

articles.headline: India's overall unemployment rate declines to 5.1% in July
articles.summary: India's unemployment rate fell to 5.1% in July from 5.5% in June, driven by a sharp drop in rural unemployment. While urban joblessness rose slightly to 6.7% due to an increase among females, the rural rate fell to 4.5%. Total female unemployment in rural areas dropped significantly, though urban female joblessness saw a marginal uptick.

articles.headline: IT ministry approves ₹7,877 crore boost for electronics component facilities
articles.summary: The Union IT ministry cleared its first tranche of approvals for 31 electronics component projects involving ₹7,877 crore. The projects will manufacture mobile enclosures, copper coils, and rare-earth magnets. This is part of the ₹40,000-crore ECMS scheme aimed at increasing high-margin domestic income and net share in India's ₹13 trillion electronics production industry.

articles.headline: Big Tech's off-balance-sheet AI spending reaches $3 trillion
articles.summary: A WSJ analysis shows that nine major tech companies, including Alphabet and Meta, have $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments primarily for AI infrastructure like data centers and chips. These obligations, which remain off-balance sheet until services are delivered, are growing faster than traditional capital expenditures and could become a significant burden if AI demand falters.

articles.headline: Alibaba to sell Lingxi Games unit for over $2 billion
articles.summary: Alibaba Group is selling its game developer unit Lingxi Games to private equity firm Trustar Capital in a deal estimated at over $2 billion. The tech giant is disposing of non-core assets to focus on strategic priorities like cloud and AI. Lingxi’s management team will continue to lead the firm, ensuring continuity in operations after the ownership change.

articles.headline: Tata Capital fund leads $30 million round in Tenet Diagnostics
articles.summary: Tenet Diagnostics has raised $30 million in an investment round led by Tata Capital Healthcare Fund and Blue Earth Capital. The funding will support the next phase of growth for the integrated diagnostics platform, which operates over 35 centres in 14 states. Tenet plans to deepen its presence in existing markets, strengthen its B2B network, and pursue strategic acquisitions.

articles.headline: Nelco to invest $20 million in US satellite firm Elveo Mobile
articles.summary: Tata Group firm Nelco has announced a partnership and $20 million investment in US-based Elveo Mobile to bring Direct-to-Device (D2D) and IoT satellite connectivity to India. The investment aims to provide seamless coverage for mission-critical sectors like automotive telematics and disaster response. Elveo Mobile was recently formed through the merger of Lynk Global and Omnispace.

articles.headline: Indian steel pipe makers tap West Asia demand for energy infrastructure
articles.summary: Indian firms including Welspun Corp and Jindal Saw are ramping up presence in West Asia as countries seek safer overland energy routes to bypass vulnerable maritime chokepoints. Jindal Saw is setting up a pipe plant in Abu Dhabi, while Welspun reports a global order book of ₹24,750 crore. The trend is driven by massive regional investments in oil, gas, and water infrastructure.

articles.headline: NCLT rebukes SpiceJet for last-minute disclosure of lessor settlement
articles.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal came down heavily on SpiceJet for waiting until the judgment day to disclose a $500,000 settlement with an operational creditor. The court asked the carrier to settle dues with seven other creditors within two days. SpiceJet continues to struggle with severe cash strain and financial losses, reporting a net loss of ₹1,138.15 crore for the first nine months.

articles.headline: Coal India eyes iron ore mines for planned pelletization plant
articles.summary: Coal India Ltd (CIL) is set to bid for more iron ore mines as it seeks to secure raw materials for a planned pelletization facility. CIL recently emerged as the top bidder for the Gadadharpur iron ore block in Odisha. This diversification into iron ore mining is part of a broader government strategy to increase domestic production for steelmakers adding capacity across India.

articles.headline: Vijay Shekhar Sharma to sell ₹4,895 crore stake in Paytm
articles.summary: Resilient Asset Management, owned by Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma, plans to sell shares worth up to ₹4,895 crore in One 97 Communications via secondary-market transactions. The sale represents roughly 4.98% of the company's total equity. The move comes as the board decides to prioritize business growth and cash retention over a proposed bonus share issue.

articles.headline: Bollywood box office roars back but OTT streaming deals remain flat
articles.summary: India's box office generated a record ₹6,398 crore in the first half of 2026, yet streaming and satellite rights prices remain under pressure. Trade experts say platform economics have tightened, with buyers focusing on return on investment rather than scale. Streaming deals are increasingly being linked to theatrical performance, and pre-sale values have dropped significantly since the pandemic peak.

articles.headline: Intelligence reveals Iran’s secret plan to escalate regional conflict
articles.summary: Leaked communications indicate Iran's hard-line leaders are preparing to widen the regional war to raise costs for the US and its allies. The plan involves unifying military command, ramping up drone production, and preparing for offensive operations in enemy territory. The Revolutionary Guard has reportedly devised plans to sabotage Gulf infrastructure and create domestic unrest in neighboring states.

articles.headline: China’s economic woes mount as industrial output and consumption slow
articles.summary: China’s economy faced a sluggish start to the second half, with industrial output, consumption, and investment all missing forecasts in July. The property market continues to slump, with new-home prices falling and real estate investment plunging. The National Bureau of Statistics cited weak domestic demand and extreme weather as key factors hampering a stable economic recovery.

articles.headline: Sembcorp Industries eyes $500-million India IPO for green unit
articles.summary: Singapore’s Sembcorp Industries is preparing for an initial public offering of its Indian subsidiary, Sembcorp Green Infra Ltd, which could raise as much as $500 million. The company is reportedly working with Axis Capital, HSBC, and Citigroup on the share sale. This marks the renewable energy unit's second attempt to go public after a previous withdrawal in 2018.

articles.headline: BJP appoints Piyush Goyal as national treasurer in organizational reset
articles.summary: Union Minister Piyush Goyal has been appointed as the Bharatiya Janata Party’s national treasurer as part of a major organizational restructuring. Goyal, who previously held the role from 2010 to 2014, returns to the key role as the party reset begins under president Nitin Nabin. The appointments include 13 national vice-presidents and eight general secretaries.

articles.headline: Maharashtra warns Bollywood stars against surrogate advertisements
articles.summary: The Maharashtra government has issued a warning to actors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff to stop appearing in surrogate ads for a brand associated with banned pan masala. The drive intensifies a food safety campaign in the state, which recently saw license suspensions for popular restaurants and warehouses. The government aims to curb the promotion of harmful tobacco-related products.

articles.headline: Diageo agrees to reformulate drinks after Indian regulator ban
articles.summary: Spirits major Diageo has agreed to change the recipes of several whisky and rum brands in India after the food safety regulator banned them for using unapproved flavors. The ban affected popular labels like Antiquity Blue and Royal Challenge. Diageo will stop adding specific rum or whisky flavors to comply with regulations, allowing the drinks to return to the world's largest spirits market.

articles.headline: Icra estimates India’s Q1 GDP growth at 7%
articles.summary: Rating agency Icra projected India's GDP growth to have slowed to 7% in the April-June quarter, a four-quarter low. The moderation from 7.8% in the previous year is attributed to a slower pace of expansion in the services sector. For the full 2026-27 fiscal year, Icra projects growth will ease to 6.7% as high frequency indicators show mixed domestic volume trends.

articles.headline: Government spending on education shrinks as family costs soar
articles.summary: Union government spending on education has nearly halved as a percentage of GDP to just 0.34% over the past 15 years. Families are increasingly bearing the burden of private education costs while facing uncertain returns, with graduate unemployment among youth aged under 25 at 39%. The gap between high education costs and stagnant entry-level salaries is creating significant economic insecurity.

articles.headline: Income plus arbitrage funds struggle to gain footing in India
articles.summary: A new category of debt mutual funds designed for tax efficiency is seeing investor outflows of ₹2,000 crore this year. Income plus arbitrage funds, which use complex structures to gain lower capital gains tax rates, are facing skepticism due to a lack of standard definitions and middling returns. Analysts suggest they remain untested over the long term for average individual portfolios.

articles.headline: Women focus on energy and stamina over weight loss for wellness
articles.summary: A growing trend in female fitness shows a shift from traditional weight loss goals to building energy and stamina. Health experts suggest that restrictive calorie counting often leaves women exhausted and nutritionally deficient. Instead, focusing on protein intake, strength training, and matching exercise routines to hormonal cycles is proving more effective for long-term health and vitality.

articles.headline: US administration has record number of ultra-rich officials, report finds
articles.summary: A Public Citizen report shows 57 officials in Donald Trump’s administration are worth at least $100 million, four times more than his previous term. Their combined wealth exceeds $12.5 billion. The cabinet includes billionaires like Howard Lutnick and Linda McMahon, reflecting a significant trend of appointing business elites to high-level government positions.

articles.headline: Trump threatens military action against Oman over Iran diplomatic talks
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has warned Oman of potential military strikes if it continues talks with Iran. Demanding Iran's surrender to end the standoff, Trump's threats coincide with Tehran's warning of an offensive in the Strait of Hormuz if negotiations fail. The escalating rhetoric underscores a volatile shift in US foreign policy toward key Middle Eastern partners.

articles.headline: Houthi rebels claim successful attack on Saudi military vessel
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels announced they targeted and hit a Saudi military vessel in the Red Sea. While the Saudi government has not officially confirmed the strike, the group claims it is part of their ongoing maritime blockade. The incident adds to the growing security threats in one of the world's most critical international shipping lanes.

articles.headline: Kushner's high-level Gaza peace talks end without a breakthrough
articles.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner concluded a series of meetings with Israeli and Arab leaders aimed at ending the Israel-Hamas conflict in Gaza. Although discussions were described as 'deep and constructive,' no formal ceasefire agreement or post-war plan was finalized. Key disagreements remain, leaving the diplomatic process at a stalemate despite regional pressure.

articles.headline: Bengaluru ranks worst in voter registration; 45% may face removal
articles.summary: Bengaluru has recorded the lowest performance in Karnataka's voter roll revision, with nearly 45% of entries flagged for potential removal due to discrepancies. Local authorities face a major task in verifying 25 lakh voters before the final list. Wards in BBMP South and Central show particularly high error rates, raising concerns about electoral inclusivity.

articles.headline: Massive fire at West Bengal hotel kills nine pilgrims in Tarapith
articles.summary: Nine pilgrims, including a family of five, died in a major fire at a hotel in the religious town of Tarapith. The blaze is suspected to have been caused by an air conditioner short circuit. Thirty-four others were injured, with some victims jumping from upper floors to escape. A probe is underway to investigate the hotel's fire safety compliance.

articles.headline: Assam proposes shrinking Kaziranga National Park's eco-sensitive zone
articles.summary: The Assam government has proposed reducing the eco-sensitive zone around Kaziranga National Park from 10km to as little as 1km in some areas. The move aims to facilitate local housing and developmental projects. However, environmentalists warn that this could lead to increased human-wildlife conflict and disrupt the habitat of endangered rhinos and tigers.

articles.headline: Mumbai court begins 26/11 trial in absentia for terror masterminds
articles.summary: A Mumbai court has started the trial of 26/11 masterminds Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi in absentia. Utilizing new laws that allow the trial of proclaimed offenders, the court aims to record evidence of their roles in the 2008 attacks that killed 166 people. This marks a significant legal step in pursuing justice for the victims of the Mumbai terror strikes.

articles.headline: Centre to offer free AI-powered NEET and JEE coaching from October
articles.summary: The Union government will launch a free online coaching platform for NEET and JEE aspirants starting October 2. Aimed at helping students from economically weaker sections, the program will use AI to provide personalized learning, recorded lectures, and mock tests. The initiative seeks to level the playing field against expensive private coaching centers.

articles.headline: Tata Sons AGM likely delayed amid chairman's reappointment hurdles
articles.summary: The Annual General Meeting of Tata Sons is expected to be adjourned as a regulatory freeze delays the reappointment of Chairman N. Chandrasekaran. A mandatory three-member selection committee has yet to finalize its decision. The delay comes amid internal discussions on governance and the transition to the next leadership phase for the massive Indian conglomerate.

articles.headline: Stolen masterpieces by Renoir and Matisse recovered in Italian raid
articles.summary: Italian police recovered three famous paintings by Renoir, Cezanne, and Matisse that were stolen from a museum in Northern Italy. The works, valued at over €9 million, were found during a raid in Parma. Nine suspects have been detained in connection with the heist. The recovery ends a months-long investigation into the high-profile theft by a masked gang.

articles.headline: B Nagendra rejoins Karnataka cabinet amid Valmiki Corporation scam row
articles.summary: B. Nagendra has been re-inducted into the Karnataka state cabinet, months after resigning due to his alleged role in the Valmiki Corporation financial scam. The move has triggered intense protests from opposition parties, who are demanding a thorough probe by central agencies. Chief Minister Siddaramaiah defended the decision, citing lack of evidence in initial chargesheets.

articles.headline: Kharif sowing in Karnataka lags at 69% due to rain deficit
articles.summary: Kharif crop sowing in Karnataka has reached only 69% of the targeted area as erratic rainfall impacts agriculture. Farmers have cultivated 58.2 lakh hectares against a goal of 84.1 lakh hectares. Key crops like pulses and oilseeds are the most affected. The state government is monitoring the situation and considering relief measures for drought-hit districts.

articles.headline: ISI-backed terror network dismantled; 253 arrested across 14 states
articles.summary: Indian security agencies busted a major ISI-backed terror network, arresting 253 suspects in a massive coordinated operation across 14 states. The group, allegedly led by Shahzad Bhatti, was planning attacks during Independence Day celebrations. Large caches of arms, ammunition, and explosives were seized, averting what officials described as a significant national security threat.

articles.headline: Study warns of mental health risks from excessive fantasy sports
articles.summary: A study by NIMHANS researchers highlights a growing trend of addiction and psychological distress among young adults playing fantasy sports. The research found that many players use these platforms as an 'emotional crutch,' leading to symptoms of anxiety, depression, and social withdrawal. Experts have called for stricter regulations and better awareness regarding the risks of online gaming.

articles.headline: Supreme Court affirms victims' right to speedy trial in criminal cases
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that the right to a speedy trial is an fundamental right not just for the accused, but also for the victim. The court emphasized that inordinate delays in justice can have a severe psychological and social impact on victims. It directed lower courts to prioritize long-pending criminal cases and avoid unnecessary adjournments.

articles.headline: Asha Bhosle honored with star-studded musical tribute by Bollywood
articles.summary: Top Bollywood stars and singers, including AR Rahman and Shah Rukh Khan, joined a musical tribute to celebrate the legacy of legendary singer Asha Bhosle. The initiative, titled 'Asha Forever,' features performances of her iconic songs and interviews highlighting her seven-decade career. The event aims to inspire the next generation of artists through her monumental contribution to music.

articles.headline: Aegis Logistics in Talks to Buy UAE’s Tristar for $1.5b
articles.summary: India's largest liquid logistics firm, Aegis Logistics, is in advanced discussions to acquire UAE-based Tristar. The deal, valued at approximately $1.5 billion (₹12,500 crore), would be one of the largest consolidation efforts in the West Asian logistics industry. Tristar operates over 2,000 transport assets and 60 fuel sites across 30 countries.

articles.headline: BJP Resets Team with Debutants and Poll Specialists
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has unveiled a new national team, emphasizing continuity while promoting a new generation of leaders. Smriti Irani returns as national general secretary, and former RSS functionary Ram Madhav has been reinstated to steer poll strategies. The revamp aims to balance organizational experience with fresh talent for upcoming state elections.

articles.headline: Rupee Slide Chips Away at ISM Outlay
articles.summary: India's semiconductor manufacturing ambitions face a double-digit cost overrun due to a weak rupee. Greenfield projects under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) are seeing costs rise by 12-27% for legacy fabs and display units. With over 80% of total project costs involving imported equipment billed in dollars, the subsidy depreciation is impacting the $10 billion incentive plan.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Board Differs Over Chandra’s Decision
articles.summary: The board of Tata Sons is divided over Chairman N Chandrasekaran’s reported decision to not seek a second term. While some directors believe the board should formally respond and request reconsideration, others feel it is his personal choice. The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust has reportedly asked the board to set up a selection committee to find a potential replacement.

articles.headline: Suntory Pegs India as 3rd Largest Market by 2030
articles.summary: Suntory Global Spirits expects India to become its third-largest market globally by 2030, following the US and Japan. The company aims to achieve $1 billion in annual sales in India by adopting a strategy of local manufacturing alongside imported Japanese and American brands. India is currently among the top 10 markets for the world’s third-largest distiller.

articles.headline: SC: Ground Airlines if Airfare Caps are Violated
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the government to finalize rules to regulate airfares within three weeks. The court warned that airlines failing to follow these rules could be grounded. The move follows a petition seeking a cap on airfares during emergencies and natural disasters, as the government had previously failed to regulate predatory pricing effectively.

articles.headline: ICICI Goes Past HDFC to Emerge Top MF Holding
articles.summary: ICICI Bank has overtaken HDFC Bank as the most valued stock holding in mutual fund (MF) portfolios. MF holdings in ICICI Bank rose to ₹2.10 lakh crore, representing 5.35% of total equity MF assets, while HDFC Bank holdings fell to ₹1.95 lakh crore (4.98%). Concerns over HDFC Bank's management continuity and deposit growth have weighed on its stock performance.

articles.headline: Mid-, Small-cap Cos Log Best Growth in 16 Qarters
articles.summary: Mid-sized and small-cap companies in India delivered their strongest earnings performance in 16 quarters during the April-June period. Net profits for the Nifty Midcap 150 index grew by 27.5%, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 index saw a profit surge of 42.6%. The growth is attributed to sharp revenue increases, softening commodity prices, and sustained domestic demand.

articles.headline: Govt Clears 31 Projects for Electronics Manufacturing
articles.summary: The Indian government has approved 31 applications worth ₹7,877 crore under the Electronic Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS). These projects are expected to generate production worth ₹82,243 crore and create 9,588 jobs. The move aims to strengthen the domestic electronics supply chain and reduce reliance on imports for critical components like sensors and displays.

articles.headline: UGC-NET Row: Over 60% Questions Repetitions from 2024
articles.summary: An analysis of the UGC-NET 2026 examination for English and Commerce reveals that over 60% of questions were repeated from the December 2024 exam. The National Testing Agency (NTA) is facing criticism for these lapses, alongside factual errors and poor translations. The NTA has since sacked 10 staffers and is restructuring its paper-setting process to ensure integrity.

articles.headline: Why Census Format Doesn't Mention OBC: Cong to Govt
articles.summary: The Congress party has questioned the central government's decision to exclude Other Backward Classes (OBC) as a category in the upcoming census questionnaire. While categories for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes exist, the absence of an OBC column has sparked political debate. The Congress argues that without this data, effective policy planning for OBC welfare is impossible.

articles.headline: Security Agencies Dismantle ISI-Backed Bhatti Terror Network
articles.summary: In a multi-state operation, security agencies have dismantled the ISI-backed 'Bhatti Network' across 14 Indian states. Over 250 individuals were detained, and more than 80 FIRs were filed. The network was involved in espionage, recruitment, and radicalization through social media. Substantial recoveries including grenades, pistols, and encrypted communication devices were made.

articles.headline: Tapovan Hydro Project Halted After Subsidence and Seepage
articles.summary: Construction on the 520 MW Tapovan-Vishnugad hydro project in Uttarakhand has been halted after land subsidence created a cavity, leading to water seepage. This is the second such incident in a month, raising environmental concerns about the project's safety. NTPC officials are currently assessing the impact and working on restoration as locals were evacuated for safety.

articles.headline: Assam Staffers Stare at 20% Pay Cut for Secret Marriage
articles.summary: The Assam government has introduced a rule where state employees entering a second marriage without a legal divorce or first wife's permission will face a 20% salary cut. The deducted amount will be directly deposited into the first wife's account. This follows the state's move to prohibit polygamous marriages and ensure financial protection for women.

articles.headline: Soldier Gets Shaurya Chakra for Foiling Drone Attack
articles.summary: In a first, Naib Subedar Shankar Ram has been awarded the Shaurya Chakra for successfully foiling a drone-borne bomb attack in Manipur. The soldier detected a hostile drone carrying explosives and shot it down, preventing potential casualties among his unit and nearby civilians. This highlights the growing use of unmanned systems by insurgents and the Indian Army's counter-tactics.

articles.headline: Ministries Asked to Form Quota Panels for Vacancies
articles.summary: The Centre has directed all ministries to form reservation committees and appoint liaison officers to identify and fill backlog vacancies for SC/ST/OBC categories. This time-bound exercise aims to ensure effective implementation of reservation policies in government jobs. Progress will be monitored by a parliamentary committee, with ministries required to submit status reports.

articles.headline: TN Received More Cauvery Water Than Its Share: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court observed that Tamil Nadu appears to have received more water from the Cauvery River than its initial allocation this year. The bench noted that Karnataka has released 131 TMC of water against a requirement of 72 TMC. The court has adjourned the matter for a week to examine the current water-sharing status and the impact of recent heavy rains.

articles.headline: Navi’s FY26 Losses Up Fourfold to ₹466 Crore
articles.summary: Sachin Bansal’s Navi Technologies reported a consolidated net loss of ₹466 crore for FY26, a fourfold increase from ₹126 crore a year ago. The losses were driven by heavy spending on its Unified Payments Interface (UPI) business and new customer acquisition. Despite the loss, the company's total income rose 15% to ₹3,091 crore, and it aims for profitability in FY27.

articles.headline: India Seeks Talks with US at WTO on Quartz Tariffs
articles.summary: India has requested consultations with the US at the World Trade Organization regarding Washington's 10% import tariffs on quartz surface products. India argues that the duties, imposed under a Section 301 probe on forced labor, are unjustified as quartz products from India do not use such practices. Quartz exports to the US were valued at approximately $700 million in FY26.

articles.headline: Joblessness Rate Drops to 4-mth Low of 5.1% in July
articles.summary: India's unemployment rate fell to a four-month low of 5.1% in July 2026, down from 5.5% in June. Data from the Periodic Labour Force Survey indicates that rural unemployment declined to 4.5%, while urban unemployment dipped to 6.7%. The labor force participation rate also showed signs of stabilization, reflecting improved hiring in agriculture and manufacturing sectors.

articles.headline: 70% Drought Risk in September: Skymet
articles.summary: Private weather forecaster Skymet has predicted a 70% probability of drought-like conditions in September due to intensifying El Niño effects. Southwest monsoon rainfall is currently 6% below normal, with central and southern India likely to be most affected. This could negatively impact Kharif crops like paddy and oilseeds, potentially raising food inflation concerns.

articles.headline: IBBI Seeks to Identify Wilful IBC Abusers
articles.summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) is proposing new rules to identify 'wilful abusers' of the IBC process. The move aims to prevent unscrupulous promoters from regaining control of their companies through proxy bidders or misusing the moratorium period. IBBI has released a discussion paper seeking public input on these indicators to enhance transparency in resolutions.

articles.headline: L&T Bags ₹15,000 Crore Fresh Offshore Order
articles.summary: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) has secured a significant offshore order worth over ₹15,000 crore from a client in West Asia. The project involves the engineering, procurement, and construction of multiple offshore facilities. This major win further strengthens L&T's order book in the energy segment and underscores its dominant position in the global infrastructure market.

articles.headline: Iran Shifts Stance, Threatens Action to Break US Blockade
articles.summary: Iran has shifted from a defensive to an 'offensive' posture, threatening to take military action to break what it calls a US-led maritime blockade. Tehran has set a one-week deadline for the US to meet terms for a stalled peace deal. Senior Iranian officials warned they are prepared to seize tankers if their rights to manage the Strait of Hormuz are not respected.

articles.headline: Nvidia to Invest Up to $105b for OpenAI Data Centre
articles.summary: Nvidia is set to invest up to $105 billion in a massive new data center campus for OpenAI. The facility, expected to be fully operational by 2028, will house over 750,000 H100 AI chips and consume nearly 8 gigawatts of power. This partnership marks one of the largest infrastructure investments in the history of artificial intelligence and will power next-generation LLMs.

articles.headline: Sebi Chair Rules Out CAS Rollback, to Address Issues
articles.summary: Sebi Chairperson Madhabi Puri Buch has ruled out a rollback of the new Call Auction Session (CAS) mechanism despite market concerns. Addressing volatility issues, she stated that the mechanism is necessary for price discovery in illiquid stocks. However, Sebi has formed a working group to review suggestions from market participants and fine-tune the system to reduce uncertainty.

articles.headline: Fewer Borrowers Taking Loans from Multiple Microfin Firms
articles.summary: The number of microfinance borrowers with loans from four or more lenders has dropped to 1.35 million in June, down from 2 million a year ago. This decline, representing about 2% of total borrowers, suggests a reduction in overleveraging. Industry experts attribute this to tighter credit discipline and improved data sharing among MFIs via credit bureaus.

articles.headline: Sebi Warns Against 'Live Trading' Tips on Social Media
articles.summary: Sebi has warned investors against following 'live trading' tips shared on social media platforms like YouTube and WhatsApp. The regulator noted that many unregistered individuals are sharing real-time trading positions to lure investors into risky bets. Sebi emphasized that such practices often lack transparency and can lead to significant financial losses for retail investors.

articles.headline: Suthar and Jadeja Share Seven Wickets to Hand India Lead
articles.summary: On Day 3 of the Test against Sri Lanka at Galle, spinners Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja shared seven wickets to bundle out the hosts for 178. Suthar impressed with 4/40, while Jadeja's 3/57 helped India secure a healthy 178-run lead. In the second innings, India reached 25/0 at stumps, with a total lead of 203 runs, firmly placing them in the driver's seat.

articles.headline: Tech Tucks Away Agentic Commerce Ambitions for Search
articles.summary: Ecommerce majors are shifting focus from fully autonomous 'agentic commerce' back to AI-powered search and discovery. While the goal remains to have AI bots complete transactions, technical hurdles and low consumer trust have slowed adoption. Firms like Walmart and Amazon are now prioritizing AI tools that help users discover products more efficiently over bots that buy on their behalf.

articles.headline: Stampede at Bihar temple kills seven women during crowded festival
articles.summary: A stampede at the Ashokdham temple in Bihar's Lakhisarai district left seven women dead and 15 others injured. Thousands had gathered for prayers in the early morning when the chaos occurred. Preliminary reports suggest poor crowd management and overcrowding led to the tragedy. Local authorities have ordered a high-level inquiry into the incident.

articles.headline: Ayush Stuns World No. 1 Shi Yuqi in Championships
articles.summary: Indian shuttler Ayush Shetty pulled off a major upset at the Badminton World Championships by defeating world number one Shi Yuqi. Shetty won the match 21-14, 21-19 in a display of aggressive net play and solid defense. This victory marks a significant breakthrough for Shetty, who is currently ranked 45th in the world, as he advances to the third round.

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs Karnataka to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ordered Karnataka to comply with the CWMA directive to release 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. Despite local protests and claims of low reservoir levels, the court mandated adherence to inter-state sharing rules. Karnataka officials expressed concern over meeting the state's own drinking water requirements.

articles.headline: Navy Gets 2 More SeaGuardian MQ-9B Drones
articles.summary: The Indian Navy has inducted two additional SeaGuardian MQ-9B high-altitude long-endurance drones from General Atomics on lease. These advanced drones, equipped with sophisticated sensors and payloads, will significantly enhance maritime domain awareness in the Indian Ocean. India is also in the process of procuring 31 such drones from the US under a $4 billion deal.

articles.headline: Suthar and Jadeja dismantle Sri Lanka, India takes massive lead
articles.summary: Spinners Manav Suthar and Ravindra Jadeja combined to take nine wickets, giving India a 178-run first-innings lead in the Galle Test against Sri Lanka. Suthar’s impressive 4-75 on debut and Jadeja’s 5-37 broke the hosts' resistance. India ended Day 2 at 21/0, firmly in control and looking to set a daunting target in their second innings.

articles.headline: Sitharaman announces reforms panel to support banking for 'Viksit Bharat'
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced a high-powered committee on banking reforms to support India's long-term growth. Speaking at the PSB Confluence 2026, she emphasized that historically low non-performing assets have put the sector in a position of strength. The deliberations focused on deposit mobilization, banking for youth, and global capability centres.

articles.headline: Meta faces trial in California over child safety and addictive design
articles.summary: A federal trial has begun in California where Meta Platforms is accused of knowingly designing features that addict children to Facebook and Instagram. Dozens of states allege that Meta's practices contribute to a youth mental health crisis and violate federal laws on data collection for minors. The states are seeking structural changes and financial damages that could reach $1.4 trillion.

articles.headline: Two Air India pilots test 'non-negative' for psychoactive substances
articles.summary: Initial results from Air India’s group-wide pilot screening returned 'non-negative' results for two pilots out of 300 tested so far. The testing follows a recent incident on a Phuket-Delhi flight. While the results require confirmatory tests, the airline has stepped up checks on its cockpit crew across Air India and Air India Express, covering a total workforce of 5,000 pilots.

articles.headline: QpiAI to Open $1 Billion Quantum Chip Foundry
articles.summary: Bengaluru-based QpiAI is planning to set up a $1 billion quantum chip foundry. The facility will manufacture silicon-based quantum processors containing up to 10,000 qubits, a significant leap from current capabilities. The project is backed by the National Quantum Mission and aims to establish India as a global hub for quantum computing hardware and manufacturing.
